/-!
# Erdős Problem 947

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/947](https://www.erdosproblems.com/947)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory
  day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [Er50] Erdős, P., *On integers of the form $2^k+p$ and some related problems*. Summa Brasil.
  Math. (1950), 113-123.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Function

namespace Erdos947

/--
There is no exact covering system - that is, a finite collection of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ with distinct $n_i$ such that every integer satisfies exactly one of these
congruence classes.

This is true, and was proved independently by Mirsky and Newman and by Davenport and Rado; the
Mirsky–Newman proof first appeared in [Er50]. See also [Er77c].

A `StrictCoveringSystem ℤ` is a finite family of congruence classes with distinct moduli
$n_i \geq 2$ covering $\mathbb{Z}$; the trivial exact covering system consisting of the single
class $0 \pmod 1$ is therefore excluded.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos947.lean#L277"]
theorem erdos_947 : ¬ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, Pairwise (Disjoint on c.coset) := by
  sorry

end Erdos947

findings.description: The docstring at line 43 incorrectly says that the Mirsky–Newman proof first appeared in [Er50]. The cited 1950 paper introduces covering systems and gives examples, but does not contain this exact-covering theorem or its proof. Erdős's 1952 paper on congruence systems contains the proof. The Lean proposition itself is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k+p and some related problems (1950), pp. 113–123, especially the covering-system discussion on pp. 119–120: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1950-07.pdf. In Egy kongruenciarendszerekről szóló problémáról, Mat. Lapok 3 (1952), pp. 125–126, Erdős states the impossibility of an exact cover with distinct moduli and explicitly gives the Mirsky–Newman proof, also crediting Davenport and Rado: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1952-03.pdf. The publisher's reference list for [Er77c] also identifies this 1952 paper.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a reference to Erdős, Egy kongruenciarendszerekről szóló problémáról (On a problem concerning congruence systems), Mat. Lapok 3 (1952), 122–128, and replace the disputed sentence with, for example, 'The Mirsky–Newman proof is given in [Er52, p. 126].' No Lean statement change is needed.

reformulations.difference: The declaration uses a finite family of ideal cosets in `StrictCoveringSystem ℤ`, with pairwise disjointness, rather than explicitly quantifying over integer moduli and requiring each integer to satisfy exactly one congruence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ideal I of ℤ is generated by its nonnegative integer modulus N = I.absNorm. The nonzero and proper conditions give N ≥ 2; equality of these moduli is equivalent to equality of the ideals. Coset membership is precisely integer congruence modulo N. The structure's unionCovers field supplies existence of a class containing each integer, while Pairwise (Disjoint on c.coset) supplies uniqueness. Conversely, any finite exact covering with distinct moduli at least 2 constructs such a StrictCoveringSystem. I proved the full equivalence with this explicit congruence formulation as Review947.statement_equiv in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the sorry-backed problem theorem. I also proved that coverage and properness force at least two indices.

sources_consulted: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/BFb0063064 — publisher metadata and reference list for [Er77c]
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-34.pdf — the bibliography incorrectly links this unrelated Erdős–Hall paper as [Er77c]
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirsky%E2%80%93Newman_theorem — redirects to the corresponding section of Herzog–Schönheim conjecture
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. Boundary checks covered moduli 0, 1 and 2, empty/singleton index types, and nonempty cosets. A genuine overlapping strict covering with moduli 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 was constructed in Lean, confirming that the structure is satisfiable. The exact externally cited proof compiled successfully and its theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; its normalized-residue/list formulation implies the repository statement. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/947 was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive user-agent headers, and only the preview and references of [Er77c] were accessible. The mathematical claim was instead checked against the original 1952 proof and the supplementary sources. The reviewed file remains identical to the specified commit.
